slides.title: Offer accepted in Laval? 5 steps to the keys.
slides.sub: What happens between the yes and moving day.

photo.credit: Île Paton in winter, Chomedey, Laval · Photo: Laurent Bélanger, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: Clear each condition on time.
slides.body: From Fabreville to Chomedey, each condition has its own deadline. Miss financing, and the seller can cancel.

slides.title: Pick your notary early.
slides.body: As a rule, the buyer chooses the notary. Late documents can push back the day you get the keys.

slides.title: Get the money to the notary.
slides.body: Funds must reach the notary before you sign. Bank clearing can take up to **10 days**.

slides.title: Two signings, a few days apart.

photo.credit: Île Paton in winter, Chomedey, Laval · Photo: Laurent Bélanger, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: Sign the mortgage first, then the deed of sale. Each gets registered about **two or three days** later.

slides.title: Then watch for the welcome tax bill.

photo.credit: Laval City Hall, Chomedey · Photo: Bull-Doser at English Wikipedia, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: Ville de Laval bills you after the sale. Pay before the **31st day** after it's sent, or interest starts.

slides.title: Offer accepted? Let's map your next steps.
slides.tagline: Let's break this down together. No rush.
